title: Deleting an index from a family and putting its value back rebuilds the family, at every index
statement: At the AlgS build position the only Nat vocabulary declared is Nat, Nat.zero, Nat.succ and Nat.rec -- Nat.le, Nat.lt, Nat.beq and Nat.ble are interned about sixty lines later in nat_prelude.rs -- so index surgery on a coefficient family has to be built from Nat.rec alone. AlgS.Index.removeAt deletes an index and shifts the rest down; AlgS.Index.insertAt puts a value at an index and shifts the rest up. Both recurse on the INDEX returning a family TRANSFORMER, (Nat -> a) -> (Nat -> a), which is what lets the recursive call be made at the shifted family fun t => v (succ t); a motive returning a family does not admit that call. insertAt_removeAt says the two are inverse in the direction that has no side condition: insertAt i (v i) (removeAt i v) agrees with v at EVERY index, because below i nothing moved, at i the value is the one taken out, and above i the two shifts cancel. That unconditionality is what lets the linear-combination split inherit its bound from the sum's length rather than from the surgery.

formal.statement: theorem AlgS.Index.insertAt_removeAt : ((x0 : Sort (1)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> x0)) -> ((x3 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} x0 (AlgS.Index.insertAt x0 x1 (x2 x1) (AlgS.Index.removeAt x0 x1 x2) x3) (x2 x3)))))

evidence.supports: Thirteen AlgS.Index declarations (three definitions, ten theorems) admit with empty footprints, asserted only AFTER Environment::get -- a missing name also returns an empty footprint. The three definitions are checked by EVALUATION at small discriminating arguments, because the trusted gate cannot tell you a definition computes the wrong value: insertAt 2 3 id must enumerate 0, 1, 3, 2, 3, where the inserted value 3 is deliberately a value the identity family already takes so the test cannot pass by matching the wrong occurrence, and index 3 must be the shifted 2, which no shift-free or shift-by-two reading produces. Two negative controls must be REFUSED by the kernel: le_dichotomy with the induction hypothesis at succ n' instead of n', and removeAt_insertAt with the UNSHIFTED family where fun t => v (succ t) belongs.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib --release -- --test-threads=4 nat_prelude::vector_space_exchange nat_prelude::vector_space_steinitz 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 18 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pinned count is 18. Mutation, RUN 2026-09-06 against a 25-test baseline (filter nat_prelude::vector_space): removeAt's base case off by one, v (succ j) -> v j, killed 18 of 25; le (succ i) zero returning True instead of False killed 18 of 25. Both mutants change a Definition, which the kernel cannot object to -- the mutated removeAt still has exactly the right type -- so the kills come from the evaluation tests and from the downstream theorems whose Eq.refl stops holding.

provenance.established_by: axeyum-lean-kernel nat_prelude::vector_space_exchange, lane invariance-of-dimension, ADR-1657 (roadmap W3-2).

notes: This removes the obstruction ADR-1627 named for the general Steinitz exchange. The route taken is Nat.rec surgery, not threading Nat.lt/Nat.beq in as deps: a dep is a NameId already in the environment and those names are declared after the whole AlgS block, so that route is a reordering of the shared prelude build rather than a parameter. All ten defining equations of le, removeAt and insertAt are iota-reductions.
